question: In what year was the Basel Convention adopted?
explanation: The international treaty was adopted in 1989 to stop rich countries from dumping toxic waste in developing nations. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: Why did industrialized nations start shipping toxic waste to developing countries in the 1980s?

options.A: Ocean transport costs dropped significantly worldwide
options.B: Stricter domestic environmental rules made local disposal very expensive
options.C: Developing nations had superior recycling technology
options.D: Developing nations requested the raw materials

explanation: High local disposal costs at home drove waste brokers to seek cheaper, poorly regulated disposal sites abroad. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h1)

question: What does the proximity principle state regarding hazardous waste?

options.A: It must be transported to specialized distant facilities
options.B: It should be stored near major international shipping ports
options.C: It must be disposed of as close to its source as possible
options.D: It should be processed only in capital cities

explanation: The proximity principle reduces transport hazards by requiring waste to be managed near where it was generated. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: The self-sufficiency principle in waste management requires countries to do what?

options.A: Burn all medical refuse in open community pits
options.B: Export all hazardous waste to industrialized recycling plants
options.C: Handle and dispose of their own generated waste domestically
options.D: Rely entirely on international aid for pollution control

explanation: Self-sufficiency means a nation takes responsibility for treating and disposing of its own waste instead of shifting the burden abroad. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h2)

question: Which of the following materials is covered under the scope of the treaty?
explanation: Clinical waste from medical care is explicitly covered due to its infectious and hazardous nature. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: How does the treaty determine if a specific substance is classified as hazardous waste?

options.A: By checking if the container is painted red
options.B: By measuring the total monetary value of the material
options.C: By evaluating whether the item was manufactured in Europe
options.D: By checking if it has properties like toxicity, flammability, or infectivity

explanation: Classification relies on specific hazardous characteristics inherent to the material composition and potential danger. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h3)

question: What does the acronym PIC stand for in the context of the treaty?
explanation: PIC stands for Prior Informed Consent, which is the core regulatory mechanism controlling international waste shipments. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: What must happen before a shipment of hazardous waste can legally enter a transit country?

options.A: The shipping fees must be paid to the United Nations
options.B: The cargo must be repacked in steel containers
options.C: The waste must be burned before crossing the border
options.D: The transit country must issue explicit written consent

explanation: Transit countries must also be notified and give formal consent before any toxic cargo travels through their territory. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h4)

question: What is a common health consequence when heavy metals leach into local groundwater supplies?

options.A: Immediate loss of vision and total hair growth
options.B: Sudden bone fractures within hours of exposure
options.C: Chronic organ failure and neurological disorders
options.D: Permanent immunity to common bacterial infections

explanation: Heavy metals accumulate in the body over time, leading to serious systemic and neurological damage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which health hazard is commonly linked to the open burning of electronic waste?

options.A: Rapid muscle hypertrophy in manual laborers
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiency from contaminated crops
options.C: Respiratory illness from toxic air pollutants
options.D: Increased resistance to viral influenza strains

explanation: Burning e-waste releases dangerous airborne toxins like dioxins that directly harm the respiratory system. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h5)

question: Which container is standard for disposing of used needles and syringes at the bedside?
explanation: Safety boxes prevent accidental needle-stick injuries for healthcare workers and waste handlers alike. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)

question: A nurse observes a colleague throwing a used surgical blade into a general household waste bin. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Wait until the end of the shift to report it anonymously
options.B: Stop the colleague and redirect the sharp into a safety box
options.C: Place a warning sign on top of the general waste bin
options.D: Ignore the action since the bin will be taken outside soon

explanation: Immediate intervention prevents potential sharps injuries and ensures compliance with safe waste segregation protocols. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T18#GNS122_U3_T18_h6)
